name: Near-Duplicate Finder for a RAG Corpus
problem: A duplicate in a vector index does not cost you storage. It costs you the answer.

name: JSON Schema Inference from LLM Outputs
problem: Your LLM pipeline returns JSON. Nothing checks it. json.loads is not a contract.

name: Lossless SQL Type Inference from Raw Text
problem: Everything imported as string. Typing the columns is easy - typing them without silently corrupting data is the actual job.

name: Subject Access Request Extractor
problem: A subject access request arrives with one email address. Finding the rows is easy.

name: Monotone WOE Binning with a Defensible IV
problem: Binning a feature and printing its Information Value takes twenty lines.

name: AIC Ranking Plus an Absolute Goodness-of-Fit Test
problem: Fitting ten distributions and ranking them by AIC is four lines of scipy. The ranking will always produce a winner - including when the data came from something that is not on the list.

name: Inline SVG Trend Marks That Report Their Own Scale
task_title: Turn it into a number people act on
problem: Adding a sparkline column to a table is one line of pandas.

name: Byte-Accurate Fixed-Width Parsing with a Pre-Flight Audit
problem: Reading a fixed-width file is one line: pd.read_fwf(path, colspecs=...). That line decodes the record to a string and then slices it by character position.

name: Local-to-UTC Resolution with the Undecidable Cases Named
problem: Normalising a local timestamp to UTC is one line: ts.replace(tzinfo=ZoneInfo(zone)).astimezone(utc).

name: Render a GFM Table and Report What It Cannot Carry
problem: Turning a DataFrame into a markdown table is one line. That line is also a lossy encoder, and the GitHub Flavored Markdown table extension has no error state to say so.

name: Read a Cron Line the Way Cron Reads It
problem: 0 0 13 5 is the line somebody writes for Friday the 13th. It fires on 61 days a year instead of 3, because when both day fields are restricted cron takes their union.

name: Enumerate Every Viable Dialect Instead of Returning One
problem: csv.Sniffer().sniff() returns a Dialect or raises csv.Error. It has no third answer.

name: Allocate a Total Instead of Rounding Its Rows
problem: A rounding function returns a number. It cannot return the fact that the rows no longer add up.

name: Report the Collisions a Slugifier Creates
problem: slugify("Node.js at scale") and slugify("NodeJS at scale") both return nodejs-at-scale. Neither call is wrong. Neither raises.

name: Report the Arrival Process a Backoff Creates
problem: backoff(attempt) returns a number of seconds. That is the whole interface, and it is the wrong shape for the problem.

name: Report the Collisions a Sanitiser Creates
problem: sanitise(name) -> str is the wrong shape, and not because of which characters are on the deny-list.

name: Report Every Reading a Conforming Parser Could Return
problem: parse(text) -> timedelta cannot answer the question people actually have about a duration string, which is not "how long is this" but "does the parser at the other end of this pipe agree with me".

name: A Percentage Column Is an Apportionment
problem: Round three equal rows to one decimal place and the column reads 99.9%. Every row is correct.

name: A Field Name Is an Identity, Not a String
problem: headers["X-Request-Id"] is the wrong shape, and not for style reasons.

name: ORDER BY Name Is a Collation, Not an Order
problem: ORDER BY name reads like a total order on a column. It is not.

name: A File Has No Lines In It, a Splitter Makes Them
problem: A file has no lines in it. It has bytes. Lines are produced by a splitter, and every runtime ships a different one. wc -l counts LF bytes.

name: A Numeric String Does Not Contain a Number, a Reader Assigns One
problem: A numeric string does not contain a number. It contains characters.

name: Truncate to N Does Not Name an Operation
problem: "Truncate to 20" does not name an operation.

name: A String Does Not Contain a Boolean, a Reader Assigns One
problem: A string does not contain a boolean.

name: A Decision Log Is an Instrument, and an Instrument Has a Scoring Rule
task_title: Choose, and be able to defend it
problem: A decision log without a prediction attached is a diary: it records what was chosen and can never say whether choosing it was any good.

name: The Exercise Works, the Matrix That Scores It Cannot Rank
task_title: Choose, and be able to defend it
problem: A pre-mortem is cheap and it works: assume the project already failed, then write down why. What happens next is the problem.
